chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from ʿAli ibn al-Nuʿman, from Suwayd al-Qallaʾ, from Ayyub ibn al-Hurr, from Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: We have already used depilatory, plucked, and trimmed our nails in al-Madinah, so what should we do at the time of hajj? He said: Do not use depilatory, do not pluck, and do not move anything.

Thus, the proper understanding of this report is that it indicates the permissibility of that, because the first narration is to be understood as referring to merit and recommendation, not obligation and requirement.

key_terms.اطَّلَيْنَا: we used depilatory to remove hair
key_terms.الْحَجِّ: the pilgrimage in whose preparation these rulings apply

ai.seo_question: If someone has already removed hair and trimmed nails in al-Madinah before hajj, what should they do when preparing for ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses rulings related to preparation for ihram for hajj, specifically grooming practices such as using depilatory, plucking, and trimming nails. The concluding note clarifies that an earlier report is to be understood as recommended practice rather than obligatory, establishing the permissibility of having already done these acts before the time of hajj.
